Test a minimal tuning: multi-band rate tracking with surrogates run through the whole chain

Source: R/astro_tune_test.R
astro_tune_test.Rd

Estimates the sedimentation-rate history of one or more stratigraphic records from all astronomical cycles at once, turns it into a (minimally) tuned age model with uncertainty, and tests the tuned records for astronomical amplitude and frequency modulation against surrogates that keep the power spectrum of the data. The rate tracker here is a fast version of track_astro_hmm (Morlet power, no synchrosqueezing), so that every surrogate can be tracked, tuned and tested in exactly the same way as the data; this is what calibrates the gain that any tuning gives to any series. For the best age model of a record use track_astro_auto, track_astro_hmm or track_astro_iterative; this function tests whether such a (minimal) tuning is supported by astronomical structure beyond the power spectrum, and which rate range (interpretation) is supported. Tests of an already tuned record are in test_tuned.

Usage

astro_tune_test(
  data = NULL,
  sedmin = 2,
  sedmax = 25,
  numsed = 50,
  age_ma = NULL,
  targetE = NULL,
  targetP = NULL,
  targetO = NULL,
  weights = c(0.5, 1.5, 1, 2),
  sigma10 = 0.05,
  lambda = 0.3,
  step = 0.5,
  omega0 = 6,
  n_sur = 200,
  n_paths = 200,
  detrend = TRUE,
  run_multicore = FALSE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

Evenly spaced records (matrix or data frame): depth in metres in column 1, and one or more proxies measured on the same depths in the further columns (no missing values). Every proxy is detrended (see detrend) and standardised; the column names are used as record names. Required, no default (Default=NULL gives an error).

sedmin, sedmax

Lowest and highest sedimentation rate of the rate states of the hidden Markov model, in cm/kyr (numeric, > 0, sedmin < sedmax). Comparing the marginal log-likelihood of different ranges compares rate interpretations. Default=2 and Default=25.

numsed

Number of log-spaced rate states between sedmin and sedmax (integer, >= 2). Default=50.

age_ma

Age of the record in Ma (numeric) used to compute the target periods from AstroGeo22 (see astro_sedrate_test); NULL uses present-day periods. Default=NULL.

targetE, targetP, targetO

Your own eccentricity, precession and obliquity target periods in kyr (numeric vectors); the longest value of targetE is taken as the 405-kyr term. They override the age-dependent values; NULL keeps those. Default=NULL.

weights

Weights of the four term groups in the rate likelihood (numeric vector of length 4, >= 0, in the order 405-kyr eccentricity, short eccentricity, obliquity, precession); each group weight is shared equally among its terms. Default=c(0.5, 1.5, 1, 2).

sigma10

Standard deviation of the change in log sedimentation rate per 10 m of depth (numeric, > 0): the continuity prior of the rate path; smaller values give smoother rate paths. Default=0.05.

lambda

Tempering factor applied to the rate log-likelihood, to account for the dependence of neighbouring depths (numeric, between 0 and 1; 1 = no tempering). Default=0.3.

step

Depth step in metres between the states of the hidden Markov model (numeric, > 0; at least one sample interval). Default=0.5.

omega0

Central angular frequency of the Morlet wavelet used for the wavelet power (numeric, > 0); larger values give a better frequency and a poorer depth resolution. Default=6.

n_sur

Number of phase-randomised surrogates run through the whole chain to compute the p-values (integer, > 0). Default=200.

n_paths

Number of rate paths sampled from the posterior (forward-filtering backward-sampling) for the uncertainty of the age model and the rate (integer, > 0). Default=200.

detrend

Remove a linear trend from every record before the analysis (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=TRUE.

run_multicore

Process the surrogates in parallel on several cores (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

n_cores

Number of cores used for the surrogates (integer); NULL uses the option waverider.n_cores or, with run_multicore = TRUE, all but one detected core (at most getOption("waverider.max_cores", 4)). Default=NULL.

verbose

Print progress messages (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

Value

A list of class astro_tune_test with

age_model

depth, time (kyr, median of the sampled paths), its 2.5 and 97.5% quantiles, and the time of the most probable (Viterbi) path, which is used for the tests

rate

depth, most probable rate, posterior mean rate and its 2.5 and 97.5% quantiles

tests

per record: r_prec, r_eam, r_efm, S_am, S_all and their probabilities

summary

mean rate and duration (median of the sampled paths) with its 95% interval, the duration of the Viterbi path, marginal log-likelihood and its probability, mean S_am and S_all and their probabilities

surrogates

the surrogate statistics

settings

the settings and target periods

Details

1. Rate likelihood from all cycles. The Morlet wavelet power of each record is computed (in depth) at the frequencies that every trial sedimentation rate predicts for the 405-kyr eccentricity, short eccentricity, obliquity and precession terms. Power is divided by a robust background (median power over depth, smoothed with a running median over frequency), and the weighted sum of the log power ratios over all terms gives the log-likelihood of every rate at every depth. Combining all terms (rather than following one cycle) is the multi-order approach of tacholess order tracking in machine diagnostics (Leclere et al., 2016) and of multiband wavelet age modelling (Duesing et al., 2021).

2. Smooth rate path (hidden Markov model). The log rate follows a random walk with standard deviation sigma10 per 10 m (continuity prior, as the sedimentation-rate transition model of HMM-Match; Lin et al., 2014). The Viterbi algorithm gives the most probable rate path, the forward-backward algorithm the rate posterior at every depth, and forward-filtering backward-sampling gives n_paths sampled rate paths, which give the age-model uncertainty. lambda tempers the likelihood (neighbouring depths are not independent). The marginal log-likelihood of the model is reported for comparing rate ranges (e.g. two competing interpretations) through sedmin and sedmax.

3. Tuning. Time is the integral of 1 / rate along the most probable path. Because the path is smooth (a few degrees of freedom per 405-kyr cycle), this is a minimal tuning: it does not impose precession-scale frequency modulation (Zeeden et al., 2015).

4. Modulation tests on the tuned records. (a) precession amplitude versus the record's own eccentricity band: wide precession filter (65% bandwidth), Hilbert amplitude, low-pass (< 1/75 kyr), Spearman correlation (Zeeden et al., 2015); (b) short-eccentricity amplitude versus the record's 405-kyr band (wide filter, low-pass < 1/250 kyr); (c) short-eccentricity frequency modulation (instantaneous frequency) versus the 405-kyr band (Laurin et al., 2016). For an eccentricity-forced record (a) and (b) have the sign of the proxy response and (c) the opposite sign; S_am = |a + b| / 2 and S_all = |a + b - c| / 3 use this sign consistency. Wide filters and low-pass envelopes avoid the amplitude modulation that narrow filters create from frequency modulation (Huybers and Aharonson, 2010).

5. Significance. Phase-randomised surrogates of the depth records (Ebisuzaki, 1997; with the same random phases for all records, so the correlation between records is kept; Prichard and Theiler, 1994) are run through the whole chain (rate likelihood, path, tuning and tests). The surrogates have exactly the power spectrum of the data, including the power of any cycles, so the tests ask whether the data hold astronomical structure beyond their power spectrum: a smooth rate path that aligns power at all astronomical frequency ratios at the same depths (p_loglik), and the modulation patterns above.

References

Duesing, W. et al. (2021). Multiband wavelet age modeling for a ~293 m (~600 kyr) sediment core from Chew Bahir Basin, southern Ethiopian Rift. Frontiers in Earth Science 9, 594047 <doi:10.3389/feart.2021.594047>

Ebisuzaki, W. (1997). A method to estimate the statistical significance of a correlation when the data are serially correlated. Journal of Climate 10, 2147-2153 <doi:10.1175/1520-0442(1997)010<2147:AMTETS>2.0.CO;2>

Huybers, P. and Aharonson, O. (2010). Orbital tuning, eccentricity, and the frequency modulation of climatic precession. Paleoceanography 25, PA4228 <doi:10.1029/2010PA001952>

Laurin, J., Meyers, S.R., Galeotti, S. and Lanci, L. (2016). Frequency modulation reveals the phasing of orbital eccentricity during Cretaceous Oceanic Anoxic Event II and the Eocene hyperthermals. Earth and Planetary Science Letters 442, 143-156 <doi:10.1016/j.epsl.2016.02.047>

Leclere, Q., Andre, H. and Antoni, J. (2016). A multi-order probabilistic approach for instantaneous angular speed tracking: debriefing of the CMMNO'14 diagnosis contest. Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing 81, 375-386 <doi:10.1016/j.ymssp.2016.02.053>

Lin, L., Khider, D., Lisiecki, L.E. and Lawrence, C.E. (2014). Probabilistic sequence alignment of stratigraphic records. Paleoceanography 29, 976-989 <doi:10.1002/2014PA002713>

Prichard, D. and Theiler, J. (1994). Generating surrogate data for time series with several simultaneously measured variables. Physical Review Letters 73, 951-954 <doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.73.951>

Zeeden, C., Meyers, S.R., Lourens, L.J. and Hilgen, F.J. (2015). Testing astronomically tuned age models. Paleoceanography 30, 369-383 <doi:10.1002/2014PA002762>

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
res <- astro_tune_test(data = mag[1:600, ], sedmin = 0.3, sedmax = 2, numsed = 30,
    n_sur = 10, n_paths = 20)
res$summary
#>   mean_rate duration_kyr duration_viterbi duration_lo duration_hi     loglik
#> 1 0.4442067     6742.356         6742.356    6315.403    6742.356 -0.4605271
#>    p_loglik       S_am    p_S_am      S_all   p_S_all
#> 1 0.4545455 0.01822007 0.9090909 0.01169109 0.9090909
# }
